description:
File: crates/smtp/src/sieve_admin.rs
Lines: 38-45

Finding: The file contains a local copy of is_loopback_addr() that is byte-for-byte identical to stoa_core::util::is_loopback_addr(). The smtp crate already depends on stoa-core. This copy will silently diverge if a security fix is applied to core — the sieve_admin endpoint is the last line of defence before an unauthenticated admin API is exposed.

Impact: If a security fix is applied to core::util::is_loopback_addr (e.g., to handle a new address format or edge case), the smtp copy is not updated. An operator running the sieve_admin endpoint on a non-loopback address with allow_non_loopback=false and no bearer_token may get a false 'loopback' result and bypass the guard. The function is used in a fail-closed security check; divergence is a correctness/security risk.

Fix: Remove the local copy. Import and call stoa_core::util::is_loopback_addr directly, consistent with how reader/src/config.rs and transit/src/config.rs re-export it.
title: smtp: duplicate is_loopback_addr diverges from core
